text:
Jordan: FYI customer ACME says the Console route card shows their requests landing in eu-west-2 but their logs and X-Serving-Region headers show us-east-1 after a failover. They're seeing auth timeouts and a billing spike. Any ideas? :eyes:

Lee: yep, we started seeing 502s and 401s after their app hit a retry storm. We traced a handful of request IDs, all served from us-east-1. Console still labels their route as eu-west-2 though. Screenshot: https://acme.s3/console-badge.png

Ana: can you paste one of the raw responses (headers + small body) and a request id? Also what region does the Console UI show specifically (badge vs route detail)?

Jordan: sample curl and response we captured from the customer:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-ID: req_20240315_84f1
X-Serving-Region: us-east-1
Content-Type: application/json
{...}
```
Console UI: route card shows "Primary region: eu-west-2" and the dropdown says failover -> us-east-1. But the route telemetry and the serving logs show nearly all recent hits in us-east-1 even before the customer reported any outage.

Morgan: quick checks: did we recently change the routing preference or the telemetry tagger? I'm thinking either stale console metadata (prefetched) or an unintended default fallback policy. I'll check LB prefixes and the route-map. :mag:

deploy-bot: Deployment 2024-03-14T22:11 by @ana: updated route-config for org:acme-corp -> added `allow-regional-fallback: true` and adjusted failover-priority ordering.

Ana: ah, that deploy looks suspicious. If `allow-regional-fallback` is on and priority ordering was changed, traffic could be actively rehomed to us-east-1 while Console still shows the pre-change primary. Need to confirm whether Console reads live routing state or cached config snapshot.

Kai: Product note — Console's badge is derived from the route's "desired_primary" field, not the current serving location. It intentionally shows the configured desired primary so teams know their preference, even if traffic is currently failing over. That mismatch is surprising to customers though. We should make the badge clearer or show a live-serving-region indicator.

Lee: customer is confused because they interpret badge as where traffic is served. They only saw the region badge and assumed low-latency EU serving. Then auth latencies went up. Billing also spiked because cross-region egress + retries. They're escalating to their infra team.

Jordan: reproduction steps for us to validate: 1) fetch route config from control plane: `GET /v1/routes/acme-corp` 2) hit API repeatedly from EU tester and inspect `X-Serving-Region` header 3) tail serving logs and control-plane events around the timestamp of deploy 2024-03-14T22:11.

Ana: I ran (1) and got `"desired_primary": "eu-west-2"`, `"active_primary": "us-east-1"`, and `"allow_regional_fallback": true`. Logs show failover triggers due to node-saturation in eu-west-2 at 22:09, then routing change at 22:11.

Morgan: root cause hypothesis: operator-intended config change allowed fallback but Console wasn't updated to surface `active_primary`. Workaround: pin `x-region-preference: eu-west-2` in customer request headers to force routing through the eu pool (if capacity exists) and temporarily disable `allow_regional_fallback` for their org while we investigate capacity.

Kai: action items: (1) UX: change badge copy to "configured primary (may be failing over)" or add live-serving pill. (2) Runtime: ensure control-plane emits `active_primary` to Console sync task within 30s of change. (3) Support: communicate workaround and billing mitigation to ACME.

Lee: would also appreciate a quick billing estimate for cross-region egress during the incident window (22:09-22:45 UTC).

Jordan: noted — I'll get finance to compute; also flagged for SRE postmortem. :spiral_note_pad:

Ana: short-term fix deployed: set console sync job to refresh `active_primary` every 10s for routes with allow_regional_fallback=true. I'll monitor and report back within 30m.

Morgan: adding follow-up to eng-sre backlog to add a dashboard that shows `desired_primary` vs `active_primary` per route and current cross-region token counts.

Jordan: thanks all. I'll update ACME with the workaround and ETA for UI clarification. :thumbsup:
